nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Fungi and mycorrhizae promotion_qna_000
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What was the main hypothesis tested in the study regarding fertilization?
nodes.answer: The hypothesis was that the rhizosphere bacterial and fungal communities would be more stable over time with organic fertilization compared to chemical-only fertilization.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Fungi and mycorrhizae promotion_qna_001
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: How do foliar fungal pathogens influence vascular plant biomass in grasslands?
nodes.answer: Foliar fungal pathogens can sometimes have similar effects on vascular plant biomass as vertebrates, possibly benefiting bryophytes by reducing vascular plant dominance and increasing light levels.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Fungi and mycorrhizae promotion_qna_002
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What effect do copper-based and organic fungicides have on bryophytes?
nodes.answer: Copper-based and organic fungicides have been shown to directly reduce the germination of spores and asexual propagules in bryophytes.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life on land|Ecological restoration|Fungi and mycorrhizae promotion_qna_003
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the hypothesized indirect effect of fungicides on bryophytes?
nodes.answer: The hypothesized indirect negative effect of fungicides on bryophytes is mediated by higher vascular plant cover following the removal of fungal pathogens.
